hero.subtitle: When someone in Lakeport dies because another person or business was careless, the family left behind has rights under California law. We can help you understand your options, free of charge.

about.title: Lakeport Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Lakeport is a small community of roughly 4,800 people, and when a family here loses someone suddenly, the loss ripples far beyond one household. Public records for 2025 show 16 injury collisions and 20 people hurt on Lakeport streets, with no traffic deaths recorded that year. That is worth acknowledging, but wrongful death claims are not limited to car crashes. They can follow a fall at a poorly maintained property, a defective product, a workplace incident, medical care that went wrong, or a collision elsewhere in Lake County. California gives a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring the claim, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and it is shorter when a public agency may be responsible. Our team handles wrongful death cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

about.ctaText: Talk with us about your family's options, at no cost.

items.title: We help sort out who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. Our team can explain where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: We respect the two-year clock
items.desc: Most California wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter if a city, county, or state agency is involved. Reaching out early protects that timeline.

items.title: We understand what losses count
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Lakeport recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Does a wrongful death claim still apply to my situation?
items.answer: Yes. Wrongful death law covers any death caused by another party's negligence or wrongful act, not just crashes on 11th Street or Main Street. Deaths tied to medical treatment, unsafe premises, defective products, or a collision outside Lakeport city limits can all qualify. Our team can review the specific facts with you.

items.question: If the other driver is facing criminal charges, do we still need a civil case?
items.answer: A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, and it does not depend on whether a prosecutor files charges or wins a conviction. The criminal case addresses punishment; the civil case addresses your family's losses. The two can proceed at the same time, and we can coordinate around the criminal timeline.

items.question: What does it cost to contact us about a wrongful death claim in Lake County?
items.answer: Nothing. There is no charge to speak with us or to discuss your case. We handle wrongful death cases on contingency, so we are paid only if there is a recovery.
